assumptions: One tenant projection, two app generations/row incarnations, one metadata change and atomic publication CAS.
Original database timestamp text identifies the row; privileged reuse of both UUID and exact timestamp is excluded. Publication retains original tenant/app generation across provider I/O.
Retirement and publication serialize at the database write. Stale cleanup can release only the original row/generation slot.
Provider truth, physical node reincarnation, later ingress publication, unbounded liveness and TypeScript refinement remain unproved.

The added owned case pairs the original app/container identity with a job generation, owner and post-resource-lock lease check. Failure and cleanup business paths beyond publication retain separate coverage limits.

Owned publication adds two job generations, two requested owner values, an identity-match input, clock0..6, lease duration2 and grace1, one pending transaction and one external resource lock. Original non-job publication bounds are unchanged.
bounds.progress: Publication and the owned database transaction complete only under explicit weak fairness of their DB continuations. Resource waits must eventually resolve or fail; physical provider completion is not assumed.

assumptions: Once a publication snapshot is captured, the SQL publication attempt is weakly fair and eventually returns either an applied or a rejected result.
No provider response, healthy state or ingress publication is assumed.
Pending DB lock/query continuations eventually advance or fail, modeled by weak fairness of finishOwnedStep.
Admission checks live job authority after resource locking. The same job/lease/resource locks protect subsequent SQL mutation through commit, even if time advances.
Provider calls remain outside this transaction and are not assumed to complete.
